correctness.rationale: The construction rounds any target metric to a lattice metric, adds a bounded finite-spectrum rigid marker metric, and uses residue separation to force every isometry of a whole nearby uniform ball to preserve the marker. The constants give a rigid subball of radius R/24 in every radius-R ball, improved to R/12 for cardinality at least eight.

originality.rationale: Metric lattice rounding and rigid graphs are classical ingredients and are not claimed as new. Targeted literature searches found no prior theorem combining them to give definite-proportion rigid subballs, cardinality-free density on arbitrary discrete spaces, or porosity of the nonrigid locus.

value.rationale: The theorem answers a newly explicit density question for all discrete spaces, including cardinalities above the continuum where strongly rigid metrics are impossible, and strengthens density to dense interior, nowhere-dense nonrigidity, and quantitative local holes.
